Inside the first world sits the source-named bus: 'one arrow that's coming out from out-of-band LAN ... split in exactly one spot' (line 284).

deviations.deviation: A trunk with three branches reports three junctions, not one split point.
deviations.reason: the frozen engine hubs only trunks with up to two branches (rataflow/src/router.rs: 'A trunk with up to two branches gets ONE split point ... Trunks with more branches keep a tap per branch'). The shipped views still show ONE corridor leaving OOB LAN with a junction cluster; no second line leaves the OOB LAN. deviations.deviation: The trunk label is 'reach' rather than the full phrase 'physical reach'.
deviations.reason: a trunk corridor has no `label_slot` (the engine hardcodes label_slot=false for corridors), so in tb every label character costs one rank-gap row; the full phrase measured extent=52x32 with 1 ambiguous label owner (specs/v2-oob-bus-a1.json), while 'reach' measures 50x30 with 0 ambiguous owners. The reach-versus-API distinction is carried by the unlabelled spurs against v3's protocol labels.

deviations.deviation: v2 carries only one plain edge plus the trunk.
deviations.reason: the renderer rejects a trunk-only spec ('the spec needs at least one edge'); the one honest edge available is the OOB LAN client relation rms->oob, which also shows the controller as a client of the wire rather than a part of it.

deviations.deviation: v3 deliberately has no NVSwitch BMC node.
deviations.reason: the source states nv-rms reaches the NVSwitch through NVOS, not through the NVSwitch BMC, and the NVSwitch BMC sits on the OOB LAN 'for power and serial console only' — so there is no controller API edge into it. Drawing one would invent a relation the human corrected away.
deviations.capture: pinned/v3-rms-api-a2-77x47.txt (four device-class paths, no NVSwitch BMC) vs pinned/v2-oob-bus-a2-77x47.txt (NVSwitch BMC on the wire)

deviations.deviation: Rank pins (`layers`) are declared in v1 and v2 although the skill prefers omitting them.
deviations.reason: measured: a 3-branch trunk cannot be routed when its branches occupy the corridor target's rank (probe-trunk-lr exits 1, 'no obstacle-safe route for oob -> pwr'), and with auto ranks the corridor looped over the whole plane (specs/v1-planes-a1.json). The pins put the device classes one rank above the corridor's target, which is what gives the branch spurs their cells.
